from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.place_at_grid(point_asset, "D2", scale_factor=0.4)

        ripple2 = Circle(radius=0.4, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(ripple1, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(ripple2, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(surface_asset, pond, ripple1, ripple2)
        self.play(
            ripple1.animate.scale(2), 
            ripple2.animate.scale(1.5),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        final_box = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(ode_eq, pde_eq), color=WHITE, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Create(final_box))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Partial derivatives act as a slice of reality.", "Vary space while freezing time to see change.", "Vary time while freezing space for local change."]
        self.setup_layout("Core Mechanism: The Partial Derivative", lecture_lines)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The heat equation models how energy spreads.",
            "Visualize heat diffusing through a metal bar.",
            "The center cools as heat moves outward."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Heat Equation: Modeling Diffusion", lecture_lines)
        
        # Use assets as per storyboard/instruction
        bar_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bar.svg")
        metal_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/metal.svg")
        
        # Setup heat distribution graph elements
        self.t = ValueTracker(0.1)
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[0, 2, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        # Use curve_updater for animation
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 1.5 * np.exp(-x**2 / (0.2 + self.t.get_value())), color="#4287F5")
        
        # Graph Group
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, curve)
        
        # Positioning in grid (using A4-D6 for the graph)
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, 'A4', 'D6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Heat flux vectors
        arrows = VGroup(*[Arrow(start=axes.c2p(x, 0.1), end=axes.c2p(x + 0.3*np.sign(x), 0.1), buff=0, color=RED) for x in [-1.5, 1.5]])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Using [Asset: .../bar.svg]
        self.place_at_grid(bar_icon, 'B4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(bar_icon), FadeIn(graph_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#4287F5")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF9F00")
        
        # Update curve color and position/data
        new_curve = always_redraw(lambda: axes.plot(lambda x: 1.5 * np.exp(-x**2 / (0.2 + self.t.get_value())), color="#FF9F00"))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(curve, new_curve), self.t.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF9F00")
        
        # Transform into [Asset: .../metal.svg]
        self.place_at_grid(metal_icon, 'D6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(arrows), FadeOut(bar_icon), ReplacementTransform(new_curve, metal_icon), self.t.animate.set_value(5.0), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Wave Equation: Modeling Oscillation", [
            "The wave equation tracks acceleration and movement.",
            "A guitar string shows space-time interaction.",
            "It models the snap-back force of vibrations."
        ])

        # Assets
        guitar_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/guitar.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(guitar_icon, 'A6', scale_factor=0.3)

        # Animation Setup
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color="#4287F5")
        eq = MathTex(r"\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}", font_size=36)
        
        # Group for unified placement
        combined_group = VGroup(eq, wave).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(combined_group, 'C3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#4287F5"), FadeIn(self.title), FadeIn(guitar_icon))
        self.play(Create(wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF9F00"), Write(eq))
        
        # Oscillating wave animation
        v_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        wave.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * x + v_tracker.get_value()), x_range=[-1, 1], color="#FF9F00")
        ))
        self.play(v_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * np.pi), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        wave.remove_updater(wave.get_updaters()[0])
        self.wait(1)

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Real-World Impact", [

        ])

        c1, c2, c3 = "#FFD700", "#00BFFF", "#FF4500"

        self.play(Write(eqn))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

            Text("Weather", color=c2, font_size=24),

        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(icons, 'C1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.7)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(c3)
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.1)

sections.title: The Concept: From ODEs to PDEs
sections.content: Transition from Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs), which track change in one variable (time), to Partial Differential Equations (PDEs), which track change across space and time simultaneously. Visualize this as the difference between a single point moving on a line versus the surface of a pond rippling.
sections.example: An ODE tracks a single bird flying in a straight line; a PDE tracks the complex 3D shape of a flock of birds moving through the wind.

sections.title: Core Mechanism: The Partial Derivative
sections.content: Introduce the 'Partial' derivative as a 'slice' of reality. Explain that when we vary space (x), we freeze time (t), and vice versa. Use a 3D surface plot to show how changing one dimension affects the 'slope' of the function while holding the other constant.
sections.example: Imagine a 3D landscape map (a mountain). Moving along the 'x' axis tells you the slope of the ridge; moving along the 'y' axis tells you the steepness of the cliff.

sections.title: The Heat Equation: Modeling Diffusion
sections.content: Introduce the most famous PDE: The Heat Equation. Explain how it describes how energy spreads over time. Visually represent this using a heat map where a cold metal bar starts with a glowing red center and gradually fades to uniform warmth.
sections.example: A cat sleeping on a cold floor: The heat equation models how the warmth from the cat's body diffuses into the floorboards over time.

sections.title: The Wave Equation: Modeling Oscillation
sections.content: Discuss the Wave Equation, which focuses on second-order derivatives representing acceleration. Use a vibrating guitar string visualization to show how space and time interact to create a standing wave.
sections.example: Visualizing a pluck on a guitar string: The equation calculates the exact 'snap back' force of the string at every single point along its length.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Impact
sections.content: Conclude by emphasizing that PDEs are the 'language of nature,' governing everything from fluid dynamics (weather) to financial modeling (option pricing). Recap the shift from tracking a point to tracking a field.
sections.example: From predicting hurricane paths to designing aerodynamic drone wings, PDEs are the underlying 'code' that simulations use to replicate our physical world.
